title: Figma client secret in an Authorization Basic envelope
summary: The encoded Basic credential of a synthetic client id and client secret in an Authorization header of a token exchange or refresh request, in a raw request, a quoted curl -H argument and a JSON header map.
rationale: Figma documents the client secret as shown once with the client id and required for token exchange and for refreshing access tokens; the contract records that both are sent in an HTTP Basic Authorization header. In a Basic envelope the secret exists only inside the encoded credential, so the extent is the whole encoded token, not a decoded secret-only span. No prefix, alphabet or width of the secret is stated and none is claimed; the client id is public and shares the envelope.

expectation.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, credential-evidence#235). Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history. Flagged under project policy: the encoded credential after the Basic scheme in an Authorization header of a token request is treated as a credential and covered whole. Figma documents the client secret and that it is required for token exchange and refresh (carrier existence only); that the envelope is Base64 of client id and secret joined by a colon is read from the family contract, and the envelope extent, value admission and generic attribution are the project's decisions.

sources.supports: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret for your OAuth app and store them securely. This is the only opportunity you have to obtain the Client Secret. The secret is required for token exchange and refreshing access tokens.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed. All values are synthetic, were built for this record and were not tested against any service. The carrier's existence is what the cited provider pages document; the value admission, span, placeholder handling and attribution are project policy. Parser behaviour, action and product attribution stay with the downstream repositories.
